device: satellite electronics BGA solder joint assembly
failure_mode: solder joint fatigue cracking under thermal cycling
failure: Documented aerospace reliability problem: BGA solder joints in satellite electronics accumulate thermo-mechanical fatigue damage from repeated thermal cycling between sunlight and eclipse (~-150C to +120C per orbit, ~5500 cycles/year in LEO), eventually cracking and producing intermittent or permanent open circuits. The failure is field-documented across aerospace electronics heritage programs and is a dominant driver of avionics derating and redundancy mass. This description is qualitative problem-domain context from the engineering literature; no specific incident statistics are asserted here (the engine's own retrieval must find and custody the evidence).
constraint: Any intervention must survive qualification-level thermal cycling (-150C to +120C), must not add more than a few grams per assembly (launch mass), must not degrade heat dissipation path, and must be retrofittable to existing PCB layouts without redesigning the electronics.

sources.problem_basis: engineering-literature qualitative context; no fabricated incident counts
